Synopsis:
The waveservants confront you when they see you come out of  the submersible. The beastmaster might be dead or not at this point, and they would have found his corpse if he's dead as it would be in the basement.They only come if you have spoken to them and they have given you the quest.You can hand over the beastmaster or  refuse and fight the waveservants. If you hand him over, they will reward you after he's dead the same way they would if you report his death before going to the iron throne.If the beastmaster is already dead, they confront you about all the destruction that resulted from the Iron Throne's explosions. Since the beastmaster is dead, they are willing to let you go if you tell them you were there for a good cause.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_BellyOfTheBeast_WaveservantsConfrontation.json: You emerge from the submersible into a scene the waveservants (Flood Tide Allandra Grey and her companion Redhammer the Deviser) expected — they only confront you if you previously spoke with them and accepted their quest. Their demand is simple: hand over the beastmaster (the "master of the beast") or face Umberlee’s wrath; if the beastmaster is in the basement and dead, they would already have found his corpse. If you surrender him, the waveservants will execute or otherwise deal with him and then reward you the same way they would if you’d reported his death earlier; if you refuse, the encounter becomes a fight. Alternatively, when the beastmaster is already dead they accuse you of the wider destruction (the Iron Throne explosions) and can be mollified only if you convincingly claim you were acting for a good cause.
- LOW_BellyOfTheBeast_Beastmaster.json: The players have a conversation with the 'beastmaster' - an engineer who operates the Submersible. The player can either be sent here by Allandra to kill the beastmaster, or stumble here after following clues from the Steelwatch Foundry and want a way to get to the Iron Throne. They can also stumble upon it first, before getting any clues about it.The beastmaster works for Gortash, operating the submersible to transfer people and items to and from the Iron Throne The beastmaster can be talked into taking the players to the Iron Throne using the submersible. If he's killed instead, players will have other ways of finding the needed information and/or items to use the submersible on their own.The beastmaster should make it clear that he would not step out into the Iron Throne itself.
- LOW_BellyOfTheBeast_BeastmasterAfterIronThrone.json: One-liner for the Beastmaster after returning from the Iron Throne.Two possible branches - one plays if the waveservants never ambushed you and the other if they did.
- LOW_WaterQueensHouse_Waveservant06.json: A waveservant working in Water Queen's House.After the Beastmaster quest is completed, the ceremony is no longer going on, so they have a different dialog then.
- LOW_WaterQueensHouse_KitchenWaveservant02.json: A waveservant that is busy in the kitchen area of Water Queen's HouseAfter the Beastmaster quest is completed, the ceremony is no longer going on, so they have a different dialog then.

context: You emerge from the submersible into a planned ambush by the waveservants Flood Tide Allandra Grey and Redhammer — they only confront you here if you previously spoke with them and accepted their quest to bring them the “master of the beast.” The waveservants serve Umberlee and demand you hand over the beastmaster or face her wrath; if he was killed in the basement they would already have found his corpse. The beastmaster is the engineer who operates the submersible (and will not willingly go into the Iron Throne himself). If you surrender him they will deal with him and reward you the same way as if you'd reported his death; if you refuse the encounter becomes a fight. If he is already dead, they instead accuse you of the wider destruction from the Iron Throne explosions and can be mollified only by a convincing claim you acted for a good cause.
